title: Find the Longest Common Subsequence
real_world_story: A plagiarism detection system compares two documents to identify how much of their content appears in the same order, even when some words or characters are missing between matching portions.

real_world_connection.system: Document similarity and plagiarism detection system
real_world_connection.input_represents: Content from two documents being compared
real_world_connection.target_represents: The common sequence of characters shared by both documents
real_world_connection.algorithm_represents: Finding the longest sequence that appears in both documents while preserving the original order

problem_statement: Given two document strings, find the length of their Longest Common Subsequence (LCS). A subsequence can be formed by deleting zero or more characters from a string without changing the order of the remaining characters.
task: Compare the two documents and return the length of their longest common subsequence.
input_format: The first line contains the first document string. The second line contains the second document string.
output_format: Print a single integer representing the length of the Longest Common Subsequence.
constraints: Documents contain only lowercase English letters

examples.explanation: The longest common subsequence is 'ace', which has length 3.
The two documents share a longest common subsequence of length 2.

expected_algorithm.name: Longest Common Subsequence using Dynamic Programming
expected_algorithm.reason: The documents may contain matching characters at different positions, so dynamic programming can efficiently determine the longest common subsequence.

hint: Create a table representing prefixes of the two documents.
If the current characters match, extend the common subsequence.
Otherwise, take the better result obtained by skipping a character from either document.
real_world_takeaway: LCS is useful for comparing documents when common content may appear in the same order but not necessarily as a continuous block.
